about.title: About Us
about.heroSubtext: A story told in four trees, ten seasons, and one stubborn patch of ground.
about.chapter1Text: Fifteen years ago this was bare sand. No exaggeration — just wind, heat, and the glint of the lake in the distance. The shore of Issyk-Kul in Kyzyl-Suu is a strange place for a garden.
about.chapter2Text: A single apricot tree. Not as a statement — just to see if it would take. The earth was worked by hand, enriched, watered with patience. It lived. Then it thrived.
about.chapter3Text: What followed was not a plan but an accumulation. More apricots. Cherries. Raspberries, currants, mulberries — every berry that could hold its own against the sun.
about.chapter4Text: A genuine, productive garden with fruit trees, berry patches, and the quiet hum of something that took a decade and a half to become real. And in the middle of it, a house that welcomes guests.
about.closingText: The garden is open. The house is ready. Come see what sand becomes when you give it enough time.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro1: At GardenHouse, we take your privacy seriously. This policy describes what information we collect, how we use it, and your rights regarding your data.
privacy.intro2: We run a small nursery and guest house in Kyzyl-Suu, Issyk-Kul. Our website exists to help you browse our plants, book a stay, and get in touch. We collect only what we need to make that work.
privacy.section1Text1: When you book a stay, we ask for your name, phone number, and email address — just enough to confirm your reservation and reach you if plans change.
privacy.section1Text2: When you browse the shop, we don't track you. We don't use analytics scripts, retargeting pixels, or third-party trackers. Our server logs are rotated daily and never shared.
privacy.section1Text3: If you send us a message through the contact form, we keep your message and email address long enough to reply. We don't add you to any mailing list without your explicit consent.
privacy.section2Text1: We use a single functional cookie to remember whether you've dismissed the cookie notice. That's it. No tracking, no advertising, no profiling.
privacy.section2Text2: You can clear this cookie at any time through your browser settings. The cookie notice will reappear the next time you visit.
privacy.section3Text: We don't sell, rent, or share your personal information with third parties. Your booking details stay between you and us. We don't use any third-party services that would process your data on our behalf beyond standard web hosting.
privacy.section4Text: You have the right to request access to the personal data we hold about you, ask us to correct or delete it, or withdraw consent at any time. Just email us at hello@gardenhouse.kg and we'll respond within 14 days.
privacy.section5Text: If we update this policy, we'll post the changes here. Major changes — like starting to use analytics or sharing data with a new service — will be announced on our journal.
privacy.outro: If you have any questions, write to us at hello@gardenhouse.kg or walk down to the house in Kyzyl-Suu. The kettle is always on.

cookieConsent.text: We use a single cookie to remember your cookie preference. No tracking, no ads, no fuss.

gardenVideo.hero: The garden doesn't rush — and neither should you. Come stay with us, walk the terraces, and find the quiet you've been looking for.
gardenVideo.paragraph1: In the spring of 2014, we dug the first bed. It was a gamble — the soil was compacted clay, the wind came hard off the mountains, and we had more enthusiasm than experience.
gardenVideo.paragraph2: But something took. A few perennials pushed through. A crabapple tree that everyone said wouldn't survive put out its first blossom. We learned that this land doesn't reward control — it rewards attention.
gardenVideo.paragraph3: Today the garden spans three terraces. There's a wildflower meadow that buzzes from May to September, a greenhouse built from reclaimed windows, and more varieties of sage than we can count.
gardenVideo.paragraph4: We don't manicure. We don't spray. We watch, we wait, we pull the occasional weed, and we let the garden teach us what it wants to become.
